name: harness-extras
description: Adds Claude Code session ergonomics on top of the baseline: a pair of hooks that carry a work summary across a context-window compaction, and a hook that blocks non-read-only Bash commands from read-only review spokes. The status line is the separate `statusline` pack.
adoptNotes: The compaction hooks install anywhere a .claude/ directory exists, but guard-readonly-bash.mjs imports ../../bin/lib/agent-roster.mjs (the baseline's list of writer spokes) -- copy that file alongside it in an adopted project, or skip that one hook. The PreCompact hook writes tmp/compact-handoff-<session_id>.json under the git worktree the session runs in (from the hook payload's cwd, since CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR does not follow a session into a linked worktree) -- fresh mode's baseline .gitignore already lists tmp/ unconditionally, but an adopted project's own .gitignore was never touched by adopt mode, so add tmp/ there too before this pack's hooks run, or the handoff artifact can end up committed. The size-ratchet gate and the type-design-analyzer agent that used to ship here are now the separate `quality` pack. The status line that used to ship here is now the separate `statusline` pack, so installing this one never touches a project's own `statusLine` setting. guard-readonly-bash.mjs judges a read-only spoke's Bash command against an ALLOWLIST of read verbs (the baseline's own toolchain: pnpm, npm, eslint, prettier, tsc, vitest, knip, publint, attw, plus git subcommands for reading and the usual shell readers), so in an adopted project on yarn, make, jest or biome a read-only spoke is blocked from running those directly: have it call a package.json script (pnpm <script> and npm run <script> still pass) or add the verb to READ_ONLY_VERBS in the copied hook. A script file run through node or a package script is not inspected, so the guard raises the bar and proves nothing.
